findings.reason: the premise is the section's whole argument, and as written it steers the investigation at process-death causes (lease reap, session exit) while asserting a fact its evidence cannot establish.
findings.text: s24 concludes that "the process running the launch ended inside that span" and that "why the follower's sweep process ends partway through a launch is not known", but nothing cited distinguishes termination from a process still alive and stalled: a sweep blocked inside `dispatch_review_for_run` keeps the claim and writes no attempt record and no report row, and both handlers the section relies on catch `Exception` only (`dispatch_claims.py:985`, `dispatch.py:3535`), so a `SystemExit`/`KeyboardInterrupt`/`CancelledError` mid-span also leaves the claim with a live process — while the section's own deliverable lists "a sweep that blocked rather than ended" as a cause still to establish

findings.reason: the node is undeliverable as specified; the done-when must name a surviving source or accept an explicit "identity not recoverable from the surviving records, and here is the nearest record" branch.
findings.text: the done-when requires the note to name "the process that ran the 01:38Z sweep", taken "from `session-hosts/*.json`, the follower leases and the producer and station logs", but the session-host store holds no record for any session in the 01:38Z window on 9 November (91 records; the only 9 November record is 03:12, project power_convertor; the record naming session a337e0e6 dates from 7 November) and the only lease store holds 74 `promotion-*` files and no follower lease — so a worker following the declared sources cannot name the process and the node has no way to close the done-when

findings.reason: the investigation's steps do not depend on that clause; it is an inaccurate explanatory aside about a sibling section's outcome rather than a step the worker takes.
findings.text: s24 states "§23 made a stranded launch publish its attempt record with the claim, so it is now datable and §19 classifies it", but §23's declared deliverable makes a sweep-launched review "reach an attempt record or a recorded refusal" at `_prepare_attempt_records`; it does not publish `attempt.json` at claim time, so a process that dies mid-launch still writes no attempt record, and §19 already dates a stranded launch from `claim_registered_at` in the `claim.json` this very run carries
